note.p: William Adams of Ham is mentioned in the Surrey History Centre K58/9/100 and 101 leases including 16 May 1789 involving himself, 12 March 1796 Richard Adams, blacksmith of Ham, is described as the brother and heir of William Adams, son of William Adams. William Adams of Ham was buried 31 March 1822 in Kingston at the age of 60. William Adams of Kingston had a Prerogative Court of Canterbury will proved on 20 December 1798 which described him as a gentleman and listed his relations including his wife Elizabeth, son William who is noted as incapable of managing his affairs, sister Elizabeth, sister Sarah (wife of William Yonge), and her daughter Sarah (wife of John May), grand-nephew Charles Brown Yonge, son of late niece Lydia, sister-in-law Hanna Marchant and his friends, Richard Clarkson and Henry Knight, bankers of Kingston. William Adams was buried 30 November 1798 in Kingston. Another William Adams was buried 9 December 1818 age 53 at Kingston. 1-year lease to William Adams of Kingston, gentleman, described as the son and heir of William Adams of Kingston, gentleman, deceased. There is likely multiple William Adams in the above records.
